title: macOS and Finder
description: Connect the menu-bar app to your API and understand what the native Finder integration requires.

sections.title: Install or build loft
paragraphs: Use the macOS download on the home page, or build from source with the repository’s tooling. Packaging requires full Xcode 26 or newer.
sections.code:
bun run macos:test
bun run macos:build
scripts/package-macos.sh

sections.title: Connect to your server
paragraphs: The Mac client reads LOFT_API and LOFT_TOKEN from its launch environment. For a source build, quit any running copy and launch the binary directly with these values.

sections.title: Enable the Finder drive
paragraphs: The File Provider extension must be correctly signed, entitled, and enabled for Finder to show the drive. The packaging script uses an ad-hoc signature for local builds, so a successful build alone does not verify Finder integration.
Open in Finder reports when the provider is unavailable. Folder creation and metadata-only moves or renames are not currently implemented.

sections.title: Use loft from the menu bar
paragraphs: Search Loft uses Control-Option-O to find remote files. Drop files onto the menu-bar icon and choose a destination. Settings shows measured local capacity, cloud usage, and provider availability.
items: Search lists remote files and reports connection errors.
Drop keeps failed uploads available for retry.
Copy Loft Link and Request Files create records on your server.
Keep on This Mac requests Finder materialization for offline use.

sections.title: Keep files offline
paragraphs: Pinned files are stored on this device and use real disk space. Wait for Finder materialization to finish before going offline. Closing the transfer panel stops waiting; Finder continues managing the download.
